newsitem.title: EGYPT: Arab League condemns U.S. attack against Iraq.
newsitem.headline: Arab League condemns U.S. attack against Iraq.

text.p: The Arab League on Tuesday condemned the U.S. attack on Iraq as infringing the sovereignty of an Arab country while the group's Iraqi representative warned the strikes threatened the whole region.
"The Arab League Secretary General, Esmat Abdel-Meguid, deeply renounced the attack, which does not rely upon any international legitimacy," the league said in a statement.
"It is thus considered an infringement of an Arab country's sovereignty...and an interference in its internal affairs."
The Iraqi envoy to the Arab League, Nabil Negm, condemned the attack against his country, warning it threatened regional stability.
"It is an American aggression, political aggression, against Iraq... (It) will endanger the stability and security of the region," Negm said.
He defended his country's military operation in Iraq's Kurdish north as aimed at maintaining stability.

The United States on Tuesday launched cruise missile strikes in retaliation for last weekend's Iraqi military incursion into northern Iraq to support one Kurdish faction in its fight against another Kurdish group.

"It gives a clear indication how the U.S. administration behaves toward Iraq...while the Iraqi government is doing its resposibility in order to maintain security and stability in north of Iraq with a very small...and limited operation," Negm said.
Meguid renewed his "keenness for Iraq's integrity and condemnation of foreign interfernces in north Iraq," the statement said.
"The use of military force will lead only to more aggravation in the situations and expose the region to factors of tension and instability," the Arab League statement added.
